title: Exodus Chapter 34 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 34 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 34 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 34.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Moses to do with two tables of stone in Exodus 34?
options: Hew two tables of stone like the first, for the LORD will write on them
Break the first tables again and throw them away
Carve the names of the tribes of Israel on the tables
Make wooden tablets instead of stone
questions.correctAnswer: Hew two tables of stone like the first, for the LORD will write on them
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:1 states that the LORD commanded Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first, and He would write upon them the words that were on the first tables which Moses broke.

questions.question: When was Moses told to come up to Mount Sinai to meet the LORD?
options: In the morning
At noon
At night
Immediately, no specific time
questions.correctAnswer: In the morning
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:2 instructs Moses to be ready in the morning and come up to Mount Sinai in the morning to present himself to the LORD.

questions.question: According to Exodus 34, who was allowed to accompany Moses up the mountain?
options: No man was to come up with him
Aaron only
All the elders of Israel
His family members
questions.correctAnswer: No man was to come up with him
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:3 states that no man shall come up with Moses, and no man shall be seen throughout all the mount.

questions.question: What did Moses do early in the morning according to the LORD's command?
options: Hewed two tables of stone and went up to Mount Sinai
Gathered the people at the base of the mountain
Prepared a sacrifice
Wrote down the commandments
questions.correctAnswer: Hewed two tables of stone and went up to Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:4 says Moses hewed two tables of stone like unto the first, rose early in the morning, and went up unto Mount Sinai with the two tables in his hand.

questions.question: How did the LORD appear to Moses on Mount Sinai?
options: The LORD descended in a cloud and stood with Moses
The LORD appeared as fire
The LORD spoke from a burning bush
The LORD appeared as a pillar of smoke
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD descended in a cloud and stood with Moses
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:5 describes the LORD descending in the cloud and standing with Moses there.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics did the LORD proclaim about Himself in Exodus 34?
options: Merciful, gracious, longsuffering, abundant in goodness and truth
Wrathful, unforgiving, jealous, and strict
Silent and distant
Mysterious and unknowable
questions.correctAnswer: Merciful, gracious, longsuffering, abundant in goodness and truth
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:6 declares the LORD as merciful, gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 34, the LORD will clear the guilty without consequence.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:7 says the LORD will by no means clear the guilty, indicating justice will be served.

questions.question: What was Moses' response after hearing the LORD proclaim His name and attributes?
options: He bowed his head toward the earth and worshipped
He argued with the LORD
He fell asleep
He shouted to the people
questions.correctAnswer: He bowed his head toward the earth and worshipped
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:8 states Moses made haste and bowed his head toward the earth and worshipped.

questions.question: True or False: Moses asked the LORD to go among the people because they were stiffnecked.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:9 records Moses asking the LORD to go among them because they were a stiffnecked people.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise to do before all the people in the new covenant He made with Moses?
options: Do marvels such as have not been done in all the earth
Cause the sun to stand still
Make Moses the ruler of the nations
Give them riches and wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Do marvels such as have not been done in all the earth
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:10 says the LORD promised to do marvels before all the people, such as never done before in any nation.

questions.question: According to Exodus 34, which of these nations did the LORD say He would drive out before the Israelites?
options: Amorite, Canaanite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
Philistines, Egyptians, Babylonians
Romans, Greeks, Persians
Moabites, Edomites, Amalekites
questions.correctAnswer: Amorite, Canaanite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:11 lists these six nations as those the LORD will drive out before the Israelites.

questions.question: What warning did the LORD give about making covenants with the inhabitants of the land?
options: It could be a snare in the midst of the Israelites
It would guarantee peace forever
It was required by the LORD
It was encouraged to join forces
questions.correctAnswer: It could be a snare in the midst of the Israelites
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:12 warns against making covenants with the land's inhabitants as it could become a snare.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD instructed Moses that the flocks and herds could feed freely before Mount Sinai while Moses was there.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:3 states that neither flocks nor herds should feed before that mount while Moses is there.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was allowed to bring others with him when he went up Mount Sinai to receive the new tablets.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:3 clearly says no man shall come up with Moses to the mount.

questions.question: In Exodus 34, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Hew two tables of stone like the first
Destroy the altars of the inhabitants
Keep the feast of unleavened bread
Observe the feast of weeks
questions.correctAnswer: Hew two tables of stone like the first
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:1 commands Moses to hew two tables of stone first, before instructions about altars or feasts are given in later verses.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 34 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 34 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Exodus 34:13, what are the Israelites commanded to do with the altars, images, and groves of the inhabitants of the land?
options: Destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves
Offer sacrifices on their altars
Build altars like theirs
Make covenants with them
questions.correctAnswer: Destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:13 explicitly commands the Israelites to destroy the altars, break the images, and cut down the groves of the inhabitants to avoid idolatry and maintain purity (Exodus 34:13, 14).

questions.question: What reason does Exodus 34:14 give for why the Israelites must worship no other god?
options: Because the LORD is a jealous God
Because other gods are powerless
Because other gods are cruel
Because the LORD is merciful
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD is a jealous God
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:14 states that the LORD's name is Jealous and He is a jealous God, indicating His exclusive claim to worship and loyalty (Exodus 34:14, 13).

questions.question: What warning does Exodus 34:15 give about making covenants with the inhabitants of the land?
options: They might lead the Israelites to worship their gods and eat their sacrifices
They will protect the Israelites from enemies
They will teach the Israelites their customs
They will bring peace among the tribes
questions.correctAnswer: They might lead the Israelites to worship their gods and eat their sacrifices
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:15 warns that making covenants with the land's inhabitants may cause the Israelites to join in their idolatry and partake in sacrifices to other gods, which is forbidden (Exodus 34:15, 14).

questions.question: How does Exodus 34:16 describe the danger of intermarriage with the daughters of the inhabitants of the land?
options: Their daughters may turn the Israelites away from the LORD to worship other gods
Their daughters will bring peace and unity
Their daughters will teach Israel new skills
Their daughters will be loyal to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Their daughters may turn the Israelites away from the LORD to worship other gods
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:16 explains that intermarriage could lead to the Israelites' sons being led into idolatry by their wives, showing the practical danger of compromising faith (Exodus 34:16, 15).

questions.question: What specific prohibition concerning idols is given in Exodus 34:17?
options: Thou shalt make thee no molten gods
Thou shalt make wooden idols only
Thou shalt worship only molten gods
Thou shalt carve images of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt make thee no molten gods
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:17 strictly forbids making molten gods, emphasizing the rejection of idolatry and the importance of worshiping the true God alone (Exodus 34:17, 14).

questions.question: What feast is the Israelites commanded to keep according to Exodus 34:18, and what is its significance?
options: The feast of unleavened bread, commemorating their coming out of Egypt
The feast of tabernacles, celebrating the harvest
The feast of trumpets, marking the new year
The feast of firstfruits, honoring the wheat harvest
questions.correctAnswer: The feast of unleavened bread, commemorating their coming out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:18 commands the feast of unleavened bread for seven days in the month Abib to remember Israel's deliverance from Egypt, highlighting obedience and remembrance (Exodus 34:18, 12).

questions.question: According to Exodus 34:19, what belongs to the LORD from the livestock?
options: All that openeth the matrix and every male firstling among oxen and sheep
Only the oldest ox
Only the female sheep
None of the livestock belongs to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: All that openeth the matrix and every male firstling among oxen and sheep
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:19 declares that the firstborn of all animals that open the womb and every male firstling of oxen and sheep are the LORD's, emphasizing dedication and consecration (Exodus 34:19, 20).

questions.question: What is the instruction in Exodus 34:20 regarding the firstling of an ass, and what does this teach about obedience?
options: Redeem it with a lamb or break its neck if not redeemed
Sacrifice it without redemption
Use it for labor without restriction
Ignore the firstling of an ass
questions.correctAnswer: Redeem it with a lamb or break its neck if not redeemed
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:20 commands redeeming the firstling of an ass with a lamb or breaking its neck if not redeemed, showing the importance of following God's regulations precisely (Exodus 34:20, 19).

questions.question: What does Exodus 34:21 teach about work and rest during earing time and harvest?
options: Work six days and rest on the seventh day, including during earing time and harvest
Work every day with no rest during harvest
Rest only on the first day of harvest
Work only during earing time and rest during harvest
questions.correctAnswer: Work six days and rest on the seventh day, including during earing time and harvest
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:21 commands resting on the seventh day even during critical agricultural seasons, teaching the value of obedience and trust in God's provision (Exodus 34:21, 22).

questions.question: Which feasts are the Israelites instructed to observe in Exodus 34:22?
options: The feast of weeks and the feast of ingathering at year's end
The feast of unleavened bread only
The feast of trumpets and the feast of atonement
The feast of lights
questions.correctAnswer: The feast of weeks and the feast of ingathering at year's end
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:22 instructs observing the feast of weeks, celebrating the wheat harvest's firstfruits, and the feast of ingathering at the year's end, emphasizing gratitude and worship (Exodus 34:22, 18).

questions.question: What is commanded regarding the appearance before the LORD in Exodus 34:23?
options: All men children shall appear before the LORD three times in the year
Only the priests shall appear before the LORD annually
The elders shall appear once every five years
No one is required to appear before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: All men children shall appear before the LORD three times in the year
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:23 commands that all male Israelites appear before the LORD thrice yearly, fostering communal worship and obedience (Exodus 34:23, 24).

questions.question: What promise is given in Exodus 34:24 if the Israelites obey and appear before the LORD three times a year?
options: God will cast out nations before them, enlarge their borders, and no one will desire their land
They will become wealthy beyond measure
Their crops will always fail
They will be taken into captivity
questions.correctAnswer: God will cast out nations before them, enlarge their borders, and no one will desire their land
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:24 promises divine protection and expansion of territory if Israel obeys and appears before God thrice yearly, linking obedience with blessing (Exodus 34:24, 23).

questions.question: What instruction does Exodus 34:25 give about offering the blood of sacrifices during the Passover feast?
options: Do not offer the blood with leaven nor leave the sacrifice of Passover until morning
Offer the blood with leaven and keep the sacrifice until morning
Offer the blood only during the Feast of Weeks
Offer sacrifices only outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: Do not offer the blood with leaven nor leave the sacrifice of Passover until morning
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:25 commands that the blood of sacrifices not be offered with leaven and that Passover sacrifices not be kept until morning, emphasizing purity and immediacy in worship (Exodus 34:25, 18).

questions.question: According to Exodus 34:26, what is forbidden in relation to cooking a kid, and what does this teach about obedience?
options: Do not seethe a kid in his mother's milk
Do not eat kid meat at all
Only cook the kid with milk from another animal
Cook the kid with its mother's milk
questions.correctAnswer: Do not seethe a kid in his mother's milk
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:26 forbids boiling a kid in its mother's milk, symbolizing respect for life and obedience to God's commandments (Exodus 34:26, 25).

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 34:14 teaches that the LORD is jealous, so Israelites must worship other gods alongside Him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:14 declares that the LORD is a jealous God, meaning He demands exclusive worship, forbidding the worship of other gods (Exodus 34:14, 13).

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 34 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 34.

questions.question: According to Exodus 34:25, what is forbidden to be offered with the blood of the sacrifice?
options: Leaven
Wine
Oil
Incense
questions.correctAnswer: Leaven
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:25 explicitly states that the blood of the sacrifice must not be offered with leaven. This prohibition underscores the purity required in sacrificial offerings, connecting to the theme of unleavened bread in the Passover (Exodus 12:15).

questions.question: What instruction does Exodus 34:26 give regarding the firstfruits of the land?
options: Bring them to the house of the LORD
Eat them privately
Sell them to the priests
Offer them as burnt offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Bring them to the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:26 commands that the first of the firstfruits of the land must be brought to the house of the LORD, symbolizing dedication to God and connecting to the broader theme of consecration seen in Leviticus 23:10.

questions.question: In Exodus 34:28, how long did Moses stay with the LORD, and what did he refrain from doing?
options: Forty days and nights; did not eat bread nor drink water
Seven days; did not speak
Three days; did not sleep
Twenty days; fasted from all food
questions.correctAnswer: Forty days and nights; did not eat bread nor drink water
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:28 states Moses was with the LORD for forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water, a period of intense communion and divine revelation, mirroring his earlier fast in Exodus 24:18.

questions.question: What happened to Moses' face after he came down from Mount Sinai with the two tables, according to Exodus 34:29?
options: His face shone
His face was covered in dust
His face was scarred
His face was hidden by a cloud
questions.correctAnswer: His face shone
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:29 describes Moses' face as shining after speaking with God, a physical sign of the divine encounter that echoes the Transfiguration theme later seen in the New Testament (Matthew 17:2).

questions.question: Why were the children of Israel afraid to come near Moses when they saw his shining face in Exodus 34:30?
options: Because the skin of his face shone
Because he was silent
Because he was angry
Because he wore a crown
questions.correctAnswer: Because the skin of his face shone
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:30 explains that the shining of Moses' face caused fear among the Israelites, indicating the overwhelming holiness and glory imparted by God, a motif also found in Psalm 104:2 where God's glory is radiant.

questions.question: What did Moses do when he finished speaking with the children of Israel, as stated in Exodus 34:33?
options: He put a veil on his face
He built an altar
He sprinkled water on them
He sang a psalm
questions.correctAnswer: He put a veil on his face
questions.explanation: According to Exodus 34:33, Moses covered his face with a veil after speaking to the Israelites, symbolizing the separation between the divine glory and the people, a literary device of concealment and revelation also alluded to in 2 Corinthians 3:13.

questions.question: How often were the men of Israel commanded to appear before the LORD according to Exodus 34:23?
options: Thrice in the year
Once a year
Every month
Every Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Thrice in the year
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:23 commands the men of Israel to appear before the LORD three times a year, reinforcing the covenant community's regular worship and pilgrimage, a practice echoed in the festivals described in Deuteronomy 16:16.

questions.question: What is the significance of the command in Exodus 34:26: 'Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk'?
options: It forbids mixing meat and dairy, symbolizing separation of life and death
It mandates cooking all food thoroughly
It allows eating only vegetarian meals
It prescribes a special cooking ritual for sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: It forbids mixing meat and dairy, symbolizing separation of life and death
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:26 prohibits boiling a young goat in its mother's milk, a law that has been interpreted as a symbolic separation of life (milk) and death (meat), a theme that influences kosher dietary laws found in Leviticus 11 and is referenced in later rabbinic teachings.

questions.question: Which nations did the LORD say He would drive out before Israel as mentioned in Exodus 34:11?
options: Amorite, Canaanite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
Egyptians, Babylonians, Moabites, Edomites
Philistines, Assyrians, Medes, Persians
Amalekites, Midianites, Philistines, Syrians
questions.correctAnswer: Amorite, Canaanite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:11 lists these six nations that God promises to drive out before Israel, reflecting the historical context of the conquest of Canaan and emphasizing God's faithfulness to His covenant, consistent with earlier promises in Genesis 15:18-21.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by Moses putting on and removing the veil in Exodus 34:33-34?
options: Inclusio
Chiasm
Metaphor
Foreshadowing
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The veil acts as an inclusio framing Moses’ encounters with God, marking separation and access to divine presence in Exodus 34:33-34. This framing device highlights the contrast between revelation and concealment, a technique also commented on in 2 Corinthians 3:13-16.

questions.question: In Exodus 34:14, God is described as a 'jealous God.' What is the Hebrew word translated as 'jealous' and what does it imply?
options: Qanna; zealous for exclusive worship
Chesed; loving-kindness
Shalom; peace
Elohim; mighty one
questions.correctAnswer: Qanna; zealous for exclusive worship
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Qanna' (קַנָּא) in Exodus 34:14 conveys God's zeal for exclusive devotion from His people, emphasizing His intolerance of idolatry, a theme foundational in Old Testament theology and reflected in the first commandment (Exodus 20:5).

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the covenant renewal and the giving of the Ten Commandments as in Exodus 34:27-28?
options: Deuteronomy 5:1-22
Genesis 1:1-31
Psalm 23
Isaiah 53
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 5:1-22
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 5:1-22 restates the Ten Commandments, echoing the covenant renewal found in Exodus 34:27-28. This parallel reinforces the centrality of the law in Israel’s covenant relationship with God.

questions.question: What does Exodus 34:20 say about the firstling of an ass and what does it signify about Old Testament redemption practices?
options: It must be redeemed with a lamb or its neck broken; showing substitution
It must be sacrificed as an offering
It must be left in the wild
It must be given to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: It must be redeemed with a lamb or its neck broken; showing substitution
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:20 illustrates the principle of redemption where the firstborn donkey must be redeemed with a lamb or else killed, typifying substitutionary atonement, a concept fulfilled in the New Testament by Christ’s sacrifice (Hebrews 9:12).

questions.question: According to Exodus 34:24, what is the promised outcome of Israel appearing before the LORD thrice yearly?
options: God will cast out nations, enlarge borders, and protect their land
They will become wealthy merchants
Their enemies will join their festivals
They will live in perpetual peace without warfare
questions.correctAnswer: God will cast out nations, enlarge borders, and protect their land
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:24 promises that God will drive out nations before Israel, expand their territory and secure their land as they observe the covenant, linking worship and divine protection as seen also in Joshua 1:3-4.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 34:27, the LORD instructed Moses to write the words of the covenant so that the covenant could be established with Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:27 states clearly that God told Moses to write the words of the covenant, emphasizing the importance of the written law in establishing the covenant relationship with Israel, mirroring the role of the written Torah throughout the Old Testament.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 34 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 34 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific command did the LORD give Moses regarding the new tables of stone?
options: Hew two tables of stone like the first and God will write on them
Make one large table of stone to replace the broken ones
Create wooden tablets and God will inscribe the commandments
Write the commandments yourself on new tablets
questions.correctAnswer: Hew two tables of stone like the first and God will write on them
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:1 instructs Moses to carve two tables of stone like the first, upon which the LORD will write the words that were on the first tablets Moses broke.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily revealed when the LORD proclaims, 'The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth'?
options: God's justice and wrath
God's mercy and grace
God's omnipotence
God's omniscience
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and grace
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:6 emphasizes God's mercy, grace, longsuffering, and abundant goodness and truth, highlighting His compassionate and forgiving nature.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the LORD’s statement that He 'will by no means clear the guilty' but forgives iniquity?
options: Doctrine of divine impassibility
Doctrine of divine justice and mercy
Doctrine of predestination
Doctrine of universal salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of divine justice and mercy
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:7 teaches that God is both just—He does not clear the guilty—and merciful—He forgives sin, showing the balance of justice and mercy in God's nature.

questions.question: How does the LORD describe His covenant in Exodus 34:10, and what does it reveal about God’s power?
options: A covenant of peace with ordinary signs
A covenant accompanied by unprecedented marvels among all nations
A covenant sealed by sacrifices and rituals only
A covenant dependent on Israel's obedience alone
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant accompanied by unprecedented marvels among all nations
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:10 declares that God will perform marvelous works never seen before in all the earth, revealing His sovereign power to act decisively in history.

questions.question: What theological significance is found in the command to destroy the altars, break images, and cut down groves of the inhabitants of the land?
options: It emphasizes religious syncretism
It forbids idolatry and promotes exclusive worship of God
It encourages tolerance of other gods
It allows for sharing religious practices
questions.correctAnswer: It forbids idolatry and promotes exclusive worship of God
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:13 commands Israel to destroy pagan worship sites to prevent idolatry, underscoring the doctrine of exclusive worship of the one true God.

questions.question: What does the title 'Jealous God' in Exodus 34:14 reveal about God's nature?
options: God's indifference to other gods
God's zeal for exclusive devotion and holiness
God's permissiveness regarding worship
God's apathy toward human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's zeal for exclusive devotion and holiness
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:14 calls God 'Jealous,' signifying His passionate desire that His people worship Him alone, reflecting His holiness and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does the command in Exodus 34:18 about the Feast of Unleavened Bread connect to Israel's identity and redemption history?
options: It commemorates the giving of the law on Sinai
It celebrates the harvest season only
It recalls Israel's deliverance from Egypt in the month Abib
It marks the building of the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: It recalls Israel's deliverance from Egypt in the month Abib
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:18 links the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the month Abib when Israel came out of Egypt, reinforcing God's redemptive act in their history.

questions.question: What doctrinal principle is taught by the instruction in Exodus 34:20 concerning the redemption of the firstling of an ass with a lamb?
options: Doctrine of substitutionary atonement
Doctrine of animal worship
Doctrine of legalism
Doctrine of self-redemption
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of substitutionary atonement
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:20 requires redeeming the firstling donkey with a lamb, symbolizing substitution—one offering taking the place of another, pointing forward to atonement principles.

questions.question: Which combined teaching do Exodus 34:21 and Exodus 34:22 convey about Israel’s covenant life?
options: Work is optional, and feasts are private
Rest on the seventh day and observance of annual feasts sanctify time
Only the priests observe feasts and rest
Work and rest have no connection to the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Rest on the seventh day and observance of annual feasts sanctify time
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:21 commands Sabbath rest even during harvest, and 34:22 commands feasts of weeks and ingathering, together teaching sacred rhythms of work, rest, and worship in covenant life.

questions.question: How does Exodus 34:23-24 connect Israel’s covenant worship with God’s promise of protection and territorial expansion?
options: Regular worship guarantees immediate wealth
Appearing thrice yearly before God is linked to divine protection and border enlargement
Worship is unrelated to national security
God’s protection is unconditional regardless of worship
questions.correctAnswer: Appearing thrice yearly before God is linked to divine protection and border enlargement
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:23-24 links Israel’s mandated thrice yearly appearances before God with His promise to cast out enemies and enlarge their borders, showing covenantal blessings tied to worship.

questions.question: What theological truth do the commands in Exodus 34:25-26 about sacrifices and offerings teach regarding holiness?
options: Sacrifices can be mixed with leaven and left overnight
Sacrifices must be pure, without leaven, and offerings must honor God’s holiness
Sacrifices are irrelevant to covenant life
Offerings may be prepared with any food
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifices must be pure, without leaven, and offerings must honor God’s holiness
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:25-26 forbids offering sacrifices with leaven and commands not to cook a kid in its mother's milk, emphasizing purity and reverence in worship.

questions.question: What does Exodus 34:28 teach about Moses’ experience on Mount Sinai and its significance for the covenant?
options: Moses ate and drank normally while receiving the law
Moses spent forty days and nights without food or water and wrote the covenant law
The covenant was verbally given without written tablets
Moses received the covenant from Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: Moses spent forty days and nights without food or water and wrote the covenant law
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:28 records Moses’ forty-day fast while writing the covenant commandments, highlighting the solemnity and divine origin of the law.

questions.question: How does the shining of Moses' face after speaking with the LORD in Exodus 34:29-30 function theologically?
options: It shows Moses' divine nature
It symbolizes the glory of God reflected in Moses as mediator
It indicates Moses’ anger
It was a natural skin condition
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the glory of God reflected in Moses as mediator
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:29-30 depicts Moses’ face shining due to God’s glory after communion, symbolizing his unique mediator role and the visible presence of God’s holiness.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight arises from combining Exodus 34:7 and Exodus 34:9 about God’s relationship with a 'stiffnecked people'?
options: God rejects those who are stubborn
God’s mercy and grace extend to a rebellious people who need forgiveness
God only accepts the righteous without sin
God’s covenant depends solely on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy and grace extend to a rebellious people who need forgiveness
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:7 describes God's mercy and forgiveness, while 34:9 records Moses asking for pardon for the stiffnecked Israelites, showing God’s gracious covenant with sinful people.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching do Exodus 34:12 and Exodus 34:15 provide about Israel's relationship with surrounding nations?
options: Israel should form political alliances without concern for religious compromise
Israel must avoid covenants with land inhabitants to prevent idolatry and spiritual defection
Israel is encouraged to adopt foreign gods for peace
Israel’s identity is unaffected by surrounding cultures
questions.correctAnswer: Israel must avoid covenants with land inhabitants to prevent idolatry and spiritual defection
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:12 warns against making covenants with land inhabitants, and 34:15 explains that such covenant-making leads to idolatry, emphasizing separation for covenant purity.
